response.sql: SELECT p.SEX AS sex, AVG(CAST(NULLIF(TRIM(l.DNA), '') AS REAL)) AS avg_dna, AVG(l.ALB - l.TP) AS avg_alb_minus_tp FROM Laboratory l INNER JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE l.`T-CHO` < 180 GROUP BY p.SEX;

assumptions.assumption: The 180 cutoff keeps lab records with T-CHO below 180; the request does not state the direction.
Laboratory.DNA is stored as text, so it is cast to REAL; blank or whitespace-only values are treated as missing and ignored.
Records with a NULL T-CHO fail the cutoff comparison and are excluded.
A record contributes to the ALB minus TP average only when both ALB and TP are present, since a NULL difference is ignored by AVG.
GROUP BY p.SEX keeps NULL and empty-string SEX values as separate groups, and AVG returns NULL when a group has no non-missing values.

alternatives.interpretation: The 180 cutoff keeps lab records with T-CHO at or above 180 instead of below it.
alternatives.sql: SELECT p.SEX AS sex, AVG(CAST(NULLIF(TRIM(l.DNA), '') AS REAL)) AS avg_dna, AVG(l.ALB - l.TP) AS avg_alb_minus_tp FROM Laboratory l INNER JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE l.`T-CHO` >= 180 GROUP BY p.SEX;
